fields.mechanism: Formation of a rigid percolation framework via heterogeneous nucleation centers that improves local sintering and promotes pore closure in the sealant interface
fields.intervention: Introduce 200 nm ZrO2 particles as heterogeneous nucleation centers into the SOFC interconnect-seal interface to create a rigid percolation framework that enhances thermal shock resistance and reduces thermal stress concentration
fields.expected_effect: Extended sintering stage and improved pore closure increase the material's ability to withstand thermal expansion mismatch, delaying crack initiation and allowing survival of over 1000 thermal cycles
fields.falsification_test: Measure the percentage of closed pores and the extent of the rigid percolation network using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) in samples treated with 200 nm ZrO2; sample crack initiation should exceed 500 thermal cycles whereas control samples crack before 200 cycles
fields.mechanism_source_span: 200 nm ZrO2 forms a rigid percolation framework

fields.mechanism: Formation of a rigid percolation framework by 200 nm particles that improves local sintering and promotes pore closure, thereby distributing thermal stress uniformly.
fields.intervention: Incorporate 200 nm ZrO2 particles into the ceramic electrolyte or interlayer microstructure at an optimized weight fraction to form a continuous rigid percolation network, and use SEM-based quantitative image analysis of the percolation framework continuity as the single predictive microstructure measurement for 1000-cycle survival.
fields.expected_effect: The rigid percolation framework homogenizes local thermal strain during heating and cooling transients, suppresses stress concentration at residual pores, and delays crack initiation beyond 1000 thermal cycles.
fields.falsification_test: Fabricate two sets of identical SOFC cells differing only in ZrO2 particle size (200 nm vs 50 nm), subject both to 1000 thermal cycles between 200°C and 800°C, and measure crack density via cross-sectional SEM; if the 200 nm set does not exhibit statistically significantly lower crack density than the 50 nm set, the mechanism is falsified.
